subjects.name: Mathematics

frameworks.version: NYS Next Generation Mathematics 2017, June 2019 updates
frameworks.notes: Preserve the distinct state expectations for each grade.

topics: Counting small collections and comparing amounts
Area, volume, statistics and simple probability
Scale, geometric measures, sampling and compound probability

tutoring_scope: Concept explanations using visual and concrete representations
Student-led problem solving and mathematical argument
Error analysis, modeling and independent practice
limitations: These topic summaries are a scope review, not a complete per-standard alignment or teaching library.
Use adult-supported play and concrete materials in Pre-K; provide accessible representations and language scaffolds.
Cover all grade expectations, including topics outside the summary; assessment timing does not prescribe instructional sequence.

transitions.title: Next Generation Algebra II assessment
transitions.finding: Next Generation Algebra II instruction began September 2025 and its first Regents examination was June 2026. The last legacy 2011 Algebra II examination was January 2026. Algebra I and Geometry transitioned in June 2024 and June 2025 respectively.

review_notes.finding: Plus standards may supplement high-school courses and prepare students for calculus, advanced statistics or discrete mathematics. They are not a separate course or a complete calculus curriculum.
An April 2020 implementation timeline remains searchable but has obsolete dates. Use the January 2023 revision and current NYSED guidance.
Mathematical reasoning, modeling, precise communication, tools and structural thinking run through every grade and course. Tutoring should elicit student reasoning rather than complete assessed work.

Schools may offer high-school mathematics before grade 9. The catalog grade scope describes content planning; it does not restrict a younger student from enrollment in a school-authorized advanced course.
